name: Autonomous motivation
definition: Motivation experienced as volitional and self-endorsed rather than controlled by pressure.

syntheses.design: change meta-analysis of randomized interventions that successfully increased autonomous motivation
syntheses.notes: Behavior effect among tests with significant target engagement; target change itself was d=0.64.

name: Behavioral attitudes
definition: Evaluation of performing a specific behavior as favorable or unfavorable.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental tests that successfully changed the target construct
syntheses.notes: Only behavior-specific evaluations belong here; broad object attitudes remain separate.

name: Goal setting
definition: Specifying a desired behavioral or outcome standard to guide action.

syntheses.design: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials isolating the unique effect of goal setting
syntheses.notes: 384 effect sizes from 141 papers; k here denotes extracted effect sizes.

name: Habit / behavioral automaticity
definition: A learned cue-response tendency in which behavior becomes increasingly automatic through repetition in recurring contexts.

syntheses.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of Self-Report Habit Index applications
syntheses.notes: Medium-to-strong association; much of the evidence is observational, so this should not be ranked as causal evidence.

name: Identity / self-identity
definition: The extent to which a behavior, role, or goal is represented as part of the self-concept. This folder keeps identity constructs distinct from habit and intention while documenting overlaps.

syntheses.notes: Self-identity association with behavioral intention; this is not a direct identity-behavior causal estimate.
Identity-habit association, not identity-behavior. Preserved because it is frequently misinterpreted.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental and quasi-experimental interventions
syntheses.notes: Effect on identity itself. Behavior changed in the same intervention literature, but this estimate alone does not establish identity as the mediator.

name: Implementation intentions
definition: Plans that link a specified situational cue to a goal-directed response in an if-then form.

syntheses.notes: Medium-to-large effect; review also reports enhanced cue accessibility and more automatic goal-directed responding.

name: Behavioral intentions
definition: A stated commitment or readiness to perform a specified behavior.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of 47 experimental tests in which randomized interventions significantly changed intention
syntheses.notes: A medium-to-large intention change (d=0.66) was followed by a small-to-medium behavior change (d=0.36).

name: Perceived competence
definition: Perceived effectiveness or competence in carrying out a target behavior, especially in Self-Determination Theory contexts.

syntheses.design: change meta-analysis of randomized interventions that successfully increased perceived competence
syntheses.notes: Related to self-efficacy but retained as a separate construct; target change itself was d=0.36.

name: Self-efficacy
definition: Belief in one's capability to organize and execute the actions required to perform a target behavior.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental tests that successfully changed the target construct
syntheses.notes: Kept separate from perceived competence despite conceptual overlap.

name: Social norms
definition: Perceived or communicated standards about what others do or approve.

syntheses.design: meta-analysis of experimental tests that successfully changed the target construct
syntheses.notes: Norm subtypes stay explicit and may later split when separate pooled estimates are available.
